books.section: The New Left, Feminism, and the Counterculture

source: original; stimulus is a licensed photograph viewed before writing (see figures)

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival, August 15, 1969. Photograph by Derek Redmond and Paul Campbell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph, taken on August 15, 1969, shows part of the huge crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York. More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music.

stem: The counterculture differed most sharply from the New Left, such as Students for a Democratic Society, in which way?

options.text: The counterculture supported the American war in Vietnam
options.misconception: Background from the books: the counterculture opposed the war, much as the New Left did.

options.text: The counterculture sought personal change, not political action
The counterculture was made up of older Americans
options.misconception: The photograph shows a crowd of young people, not older Americans.

options.text: The counterculture defended the values of the suburbs
options.misconception: The counterculture rejected suburban middle-class values, so it did not defend them.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the counterculture opposed the war, much as the New Left did.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the counterculture sought a personal revolution through music, dress, and drugs, while the New Left sought political change.
rationales.C: The photograph shows a crowd of young people, not older Americans.
rationales.D: The counterculture rejected suburban middle-class values, so it did not defend them.
rationales.general:
1. Background from the books: the New Left marched, organized, and demanded political change.
2. Background from the books: the counterculture turned inward, to long hair, rock music, drugs, and communal living.
3. Background from the books: one group tried to change the government; the other tried to change how a person lived.
Remember: Two movements can share enemies and still differ in whether they seek political or personal change.
